content.text:
I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral table, and all six figure briefs, building a full source ledger against the disclosure and the affirmative USER passages in the conversation.

**Ledger result (traced, no unsupported technical matter found):**

- **Claims 1–20** — every limitation traces: rigid base with first/second sides, motor coupled to the first side, extraction mechanism on the first side in fluid communication with the second-side chamber, rigid low-friction loop/skirt at the perimeter (plastic, metal, PTFE, combinations), "not intended to form a complete airtight seal," air entering beneath the perimeter, continuous extraction maintaining sub-atmospheric chamber, pressure differential holding without operator downforce, rigid path with substantially less damping than a flexible suction cup, low-friction sliding while the vacuum maintains contact, guiding handles, rope/wire/cable pulling element with decoupled control. Claim 10 (stirring elements causing constant forward motion) traces to the USER message adding autonomous mode.
- **Numerals 10–48** — each denotes one part, each is used in the description, and each appears on at least one sheet; figure numeral lists match the bodies of their briefs.
- **Figure briefs** — generic slab/block/band/ring/column outlines are declared schematic and are matched by shape-neutral claims and description; the FIG. 4 bearing-face shape and the FIG. 2 port are disclaimed inside the briefs only, and no "by way of example" or "any closed outline" broadening leaks into the Brief Description or detailed description. Section designations 2-2 and 4-4 are consistent across FIG. 3, FIG. 2, FIG. 4, and the Brief Description.
- No drafting notes, placeholders, questions, or instructions to a person remain in any draft section.

**One item to fix:** the FIG. 3 brief affirmatively declares the circumferential position at which each section line crosses the perimeter member to be arbitrary, while FIG. 4 (and the Brief Description) identify line 4-4 as passing through a place where the clearance is present — a functional-interface position statement that cannot also be arbitrary.

p.summary: Full source ledger built and traced. Every limitation of claims 1-20 (rigid base with first and second sides; vibration motor coupled to the first side; air-extraction mechanism on the first side in fluid communication with a second-side chamber; rigid low-friction perimeter member of plastic, metal, PTFE or a combination of rigid materials; no complete airtight seal; clearance admitting ambient air along at least part of the member; continuous extraction maintaining the chamber below atmospheric pressure; pressure differential holding the device without operator downforce; all-rigid vibration transmission path with no elastomeric, foam or resilient mount; sliding over the exposed face while the differential is maintained; guiding handle; rope, wire or cable pulling element with decoupled control; and the stirring elements causing constant forward motion) was traced to an exact affirmative passage in input/disclosure.md or to the USER conversation message adding autonomous mode. All seventeen numbered parts (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 34, 36, 38, 40, 42, 44, 46, 48) were checked: each denotes one part only, each is used in the detailed description, and each appears on at least one sheet, with every per-figure numeral list matching the identifications in the body of its brief. All six figure briefs and all six Brief Description paragraphs were checked against each other and against the description: the generic slab, block, band, ring and column outlines are declared schematic, the claims and description remain shape-neutral, the FIG. 4 bearing-face form and the FIG. 2 port are disclaimed inside the briefs only, and no 'by way of example' or 'any closed outline' broadening leaks into the application text. Section designations 2-2 and 4-4 are used identically in FIG. 3, in the FIG. 2 and FIG. 4 view briefs, and in the Brief Description. No drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains in any draft section, and the Background prior-art characterizations were left for the later citation review. One internal inconsistency between drawing specifications was verified and is reported: the FIG. 3 brief declares the circumferential position at which each section line crosses the perimeter member to be a placement convention, while the FIG. 4 brief and the Brief Description identify line 4-4 as taken at a place along the perimeter member where the clearance is present, which is a substantive position statement about the bearing interface and cannot simultaneously be arbitrary.

findings.title: FIG. 3 declares the section-line angular position on the perimeter member arbitrary, while FIG. 4 relies on line 4-4 being at a place where the clearance is present
findings.where: figures/FIG-3-BOTTOM-PLAN-VIEW-OF-THE-VIBRATION-DEVICE.md, 'Geometry to be drawn', final sentence of the section-line paragraph; cross-read with figures/FIG-4-ENLARGED-SECTION-OF-THE-PERIMETER-MEMBER-END.md 'View' line and draft/07-drawings.md, FIG. 4 paragraph
findings.detail: The FIG. 3 brief affirmatively states that the circumferential position at which each section line crosses the perimeter member ring is arbitrary. The FIG. 4 brief and the Brief Description, however, both identify line 4-4 as taken at a specific place along the perimeter member selected because the clearance is present there, and the FIG. 2 brief takes line 2-2 where the perimeter member bears on the covering element. Where the clearance remains only 'along at least part of the perimeter member', as the description and every independent claim recite, the circumferential position at which the section plane crosses the loop determines the interface condition shown; it therefore cannot also be declared a free placement convention. This is a circumferential end-position statement about a functional bearing and flow interface, so it is substantive notwithstanding the schematic disclaimer. The conflict is between drawing specifications only; the underlying substance ('a clearance 34 remains ... along at least part of the perimeter member 24') is supported by the disclosure passage 'it restricts airflow into the chamber while maintaining rigid contact with the tile. The air-extraction mechanism continuously removes air entering beneath the rigid perimeter'.
findings.evidence: FIG. 3 brief: 'Their drawn positions, including the angular position at which each crosses the ring, are a placement convention for this sheet only.' FIG. 4 brief, View: 'Enlarged fragmentary section taken on line 4-4 of FIG. 3, through the lower end of the perimeter member where the clearance is present.' draft/07-drawings.md: 'FIG. 4 is an enlarged fragmentary sectional view taken on line 4-4 of FIG. 3, at a place along the perimeter member where the clearance is present ...' draft/08-detailed-description.md: 'a clearance 34 remains between the bearing face 26 and the exposed face 38 along at least part of the perimeter member 24, as shown enlarged in FIG. 4.'
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-3-BOTTOM-PLAN-VIEW-OF-THE-VIBRATION-DEVICE.md, replace the sentence 'Their drawn positions, including the angular position at which each crosses the ring, are a placement convention for this sheet only.' with 'Where each line is drawn on this sheet is a placement convention for this sheet only.' No other brief, claim, numeral definition or application text changes; the FIG. 4 view line and the FIG. 4 paragraph of the Brief Description stand as written.
